answer: Each identity holds one distinct irrigation share tied to an intake jetty on its island district, verified monthly when the ditch rider logs real flow to that share during nectar bloom. Shares trade rarely, cost about $4,000 each plus $260 yearly assessment; one share serves one identity, flow logs are cross-checked against pump meters, a cloned share is refused and its 5-coin bond is lost. 1,000 Sybils need 1,000 separate shares ($4 million) in closed systems that seldom sell. Trade-off: arid-region agents qualify slowly.
